Name: Gorgon
Source: Lyres Guide to Risk and Reward
Information:
**Gorgon**

During the first age, many mortals were granted eternal beauty and life by the Eidolons so they could aid the Eidolons in the management of various places of interest. These mortals were intended to serve as the Eidolon’s proxies, students, and representatives as the gods retreated behind the Divine Curtain, and many of these individuals used their eternal life to learn powerful magic, or used their new divine power as a source of sorcery. However, during the War in One Moment many of these eternal proxies turned to the side of Mnemosyne and the Twilight Authority. Following their defeat, these traitorous proxies were punished for lending their nations’ resources to the wrong cause: they were cursed to take the form of massive monstrous beasts that turned those who looked upon them to stone. When the war ended the Eidolons sought to relieve the other proxies of their duties, and those who resisted were also turned into gorgons. Now, these gorgons exist in secret pockets across Somnus Domina.

***The Traitor of Mot.*** One such gorgon is Lady Tomyris - a sorceress who ruled a city that once stood where Mot now stands. She was a student of Vestias herself, but turned her city over to Mnemosyne to be one of the key points in the Eternal Moment ritual. When Vestias discovered this she turned her god-trapping superweapon against Mnemosyne and cursed both Lady Tomyris and her people. Long before, however, Lady Tomyris had made a sacred pact with the Eidolons that stated her city would persist eternally under her rule so long as she lived; this promise was kept, and as Tomyris was turned into a gorgon, her city was plunged underground, fated to always exist within the earth so long as she did. She now rules the caverns and pockets of the decaying city below Summergrass.

***Unrelenting Nostalgia.*** Gorgons are obsessed with their former beauty and status. Their monstrous minds latch onto their old life, often convincing them they can retake what they lost. Gorgons lay claim to territory to make themselves feel powerful, and form cults, courts, harems and families that help them feel less like the monster they have become. Those who had no malice in their hearts but refused to relinquish their gifts often go mad with sorrow, turning into wild monsters that seek to devour any mortal they feel is more fortunate than them.

**Curse of a Gorgon’s Heart**

If a creature is granted the unbridled affection of a gorgon, they are cursed to suffer. Such a creature is slowly petrified over their life, the length of which is reduced by one additional year for each year that passes. They suffer a -2 penalty to all of their ability scores, and they have disadvantage on saving throws made to avoid being petrified. A creature can avoid this curse by rebuffing a gorgon’s love to the extent that it breaks their heart, or if the gorgon expresses their affection through destructive means. This curse leads most gorgons to seek affection and companionship through relationships they can intentionally abuse, so their cruelty protects the subjects of their attention. Alternatively many form a heartless harem, choosing to see individuals as food and entertainment instead of as unique people.

**Gorgon’s Lair**

A gorgon’s lair is usually hidden deep within the earth, or are the ruins of a place that was important to them when they were mortal. It will usually choose to inhabit and use its lair in its humanoid form, but will ensure the setting is suitable for its larger monstrous form to move about and defend itself in. A gorgon will usually appoint their lair with statues of those unlucky enough to have been close to it in life, who it is likely to have petrified during its wretched eternal life. Knowing the threat they pose, a gorgon will remove mirrors and reflective surfaces from their lair unless they are in dimly lit places or feature unclear reflective surfaces.

Stat Blocks.title: Gorgon
languages: languages it spoke during its mortal life (usually Common or Elvish)

traits.name: Petrifying Gaze
traits.description: When a creature that can see the gorgon’s eyes starts their turn within 30 feet of it, the gorgon can force them to make a DC 19 Constitution saving throw (unless the gorgon is incapacitated). If the target fails by 5 points or more, they are instantly petrified. If they fail by less, then they begin to turn to stone and are restrained. While restrained this way they must repeat the saving throw at the end of their next turn, becoming petrified on a failure or ending the effect on a success. The petrification lasts until the gorgon dies, greater restoration is cast on the creature, or the gorgon uses an action to restore the target. Unless surprised, a creature can avert their eyes at the start of their turn to avoid the saving throw, but in doing so are blinded to the gorgon or anything in its direction until the start of their next turn. If the gorgon sees itself reflected in a surface within 30 feet while in bright light it makes a save (with advantage) against its own Petrifying Gaze.

traits.name: Stone Aura
traits.description: While the gorgon is in its true form, every foot a creature (except the gorgon) moves within 30 feet of the gorgon costs twice as many feet unless they are immune or resistant to being petrified.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The Gorgon makes two Claw attacks, then uses their Eye of Stoneculling or Tail once.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +12 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) poison damage.

actions.name: Tail (True Form Only)
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +12 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 44 (6d12 + 5) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Eye of Stoneculling
actions.description: One creature within 120 feet that the gorgon chooses and who can see the gorgon must make a DC 19 Constitution saving throw, taking 4d12 psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. If the target fails the save by 5 points or more they are partially petrified (creatures immune to being petrified are unaffected) for 1 hour. Creatures partially petrified this way can only take 1 action or bonus action on their turn (but not both), their speed is reduced to 10 feet and cannot be increased, and they cannot take reactions. They can repeat this save at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on a success.

bonus_actions.name: Shapechange
bonus_actions.description: The gorgon transforms into a Medium humanoid appearance (that it would have held before succumbing to its curse) or back to its true form. Apart from its size, it retains the same statistics between both forms.

options.name: Detect
options.description: The gorgon makes a Wisdom (Perception) check.

options.name: Tail Attack
options.description: The gorgon makes a Tail attack.

options.name: Nightmare Wave (Costs 2 Actions)
options.description: The gorgon subjects up to three creatures it can see within 60 feet to visions of its own tormented existence, forcing them to each make a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, the targets take 13 (2d12) psychic damage and have disadvantage on weapon attacks until the start of the gorgon’s next turn.

legendary_reactions.source_conversion_note: Converted from Legendary Resistance (3/Day) per standing formatting rule.

lair_actions.intro: On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the gorgon can take a lair action to cause one of the following effects. They cannot use the same effect two rounds in a row.

options.name: Ancient Scream
options.description: A horrific wail erupts through the lair, forcing all creatures in a 10-foot to 50-foot-radius sphere centered on a point the gorgon chooses to make a DC 16 Constitution saving throw. Any creature that fails takes 14 (3d8) psychic damage and loses concentration on any effects they are focusing on.

options.name: Mineral Soldiers
options.description: Stone humanoids erupt from the earth in three spaces the gorgon chooses within 120 feet. Each has a 5 foot reach, and each time a creature leaves that reach they make an attack against the creature, using the gorgon’s Claw attack and damage.

options.name: Uneven Earth
options.description: All ground in the lair becomes uneven until initiative count 20 the following round. Any creature moving along a surface who does not have a climb speed treats all movement as if it is through difficult terrain.
